newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall, investors brace for Friday's jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall, investors brace for Friday's jobs report.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell in light trading Thursday as investors were unwilling to make big bets ahead of Friday's key jobs report for August.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 22.20 points at 5,634.70. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 13-7 on trading of 204 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 9.74 to 1,134.08. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.96 to 559.30.

Wall Street may have gotten a taste of what to expect in Friday's monthly jobs numbers as the Labour Department reported that new applications for unemployment benefits fell by an unexpectedly sharp 15,000 last week, ending four straight weeks of rises.
The jobless claims for the week ended Aug. 31 fell to 316,000 from 331,000 in the prior week. They had been expected at about 335,000.
The concern is that a strong jobs report coupled with rising wages could prompt the inflation-sensitive Federal Reserve to boost interest rates, analysts said.
The Fed, which will hold a policy-setting meeting on Sept. 24, has kept interest rates unchanged since it last cut them in January by one-quarter of a percentage point.

"No one's making any big commitments before the data tomorrow ... I expect we'll hover around zero for the rest of the day on light volume," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co.

"It's a waiting game. The signs are the economy is stronger than we expected, which means earnings will be good, but the Fed could tighten," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at PanAgora Asset Management.
"As long as that's in the cards, there will be a lot of volatility and uncertainty, and people aren't going to be trading," he said.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off more than half a point and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, rose to 7.15 percent from 7.10 percent at Wednesday's close.
The shares of retailers were in the spotlight as they reported their August sales.
The Gap Inc. fell 4-7/8 to 29 in active trade after posting flat same-store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year.
The Limited Inc. fell 1-1/8 to 17-5/8 and its spin-off Intimate Brands Inc. dropped 1-7/8 to 18-1/4. Both reported August same store sales up only 2 percent.
Polaris Industries Inc. dove 4-5/8 to 23-5/8. Late Wednesday, its said that sales of motorized water vehicles fell in the eight months ended in August.
Zilog Inc. plummeted more than 35 percent, off 8-3/8 to 15-1/2 after the maker of integrated computer circuits said it expected weak third quarter results.
